the horizontal and vertical projection of a pattern can be used to uniquely identify the original pattern and to reconstruct it.
(1) A pattern is reconstructable if and only if its horizontal and vertical projections are equal, and (2) the original pattern can be reconstructed in time m × n.
a binary pattern can be reconstructed from its projections if and only if its projection graph is a tree.

the following problem: given the horizontal and vertical projection functions of a binary pattern, can we reconstruct the binary pattern?
the reconstruction of binary patterns in terms of their horizontal and vertical projections.
the following problem: Given the horizontal and the vertical projection of a finite binary matrix f, can we reconstruct f?

any pattern can be reconstructed in time m×n from its projections.
any binary pattern can be perfectly or approximately reconstructed in time o(n2) where n is the number of elements in the pattern.
a pattern can be reconstructed from its projections in polynomial time.

the reconstruction of a pattern is a process that can be accomplished by a simple algorithm.
